See also: escòla and escolà

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Latin schola, from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”). First attested in the 14th century.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [əsˈkɔ.lə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [esˈkɔ.la]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔla

Noun

[edit]

escola f (plural escoles)

  1. school
Related terms
[edit]
  • escolar

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “escola”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026

Further reading

[edit]
  • “escola”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “escola” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “escola” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

escola

  1. inflection of escolar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese escola (13th century, Cantigas de Santa Maria), from Latin schola, from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /esˈkɔla/ [ɪs̺ˈkɔ.lɐ]
  • Rhymes: -ɔla
  • Hyphenation: es‧co‧la

Noun

[edit]

escola f (plural escolas)

  1. school
    • 1707, Salvador Francisco Roel, Entremés ao real e feliz parto da nosa raíña:
      Afonso:
      E como està o afillado?
      Christobo:
      Esse jà quer ir a Escola,
      pero porque non tèn sayo
      està decote na Eyra
      para escorrentar o Gando.
      Afonso:
      Pois esso non e ben feyto,
      porque e vivo coma vn allo,
      fino coma vnha pimenta,
      e se quer ser Lecenceado
      an que venda os bois do jugo
      lle teño de dar estado.
      Afonso:
      How is doing my godchild?
      Christobo:
      He already want to go to school,
      but since he has no robe
      is all the time in the field
      to drive away the livestock.
      Afonso:
      But this is not correct,
      because he is smart as a whip,
      acute as a pepper grain,
      and if he wants to be a bachelor,
      even if I have to sell the yoke oxen,
      I ought to give him estate.
  2. academy
  3. college

Related terms

[edit]
  • escolar
  • escoler
  • mestrescola

References

[edit]
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “escola”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “escola”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “escola”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “escola”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “escola”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
escola
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese escola, from Latin schola, from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ, “spare time, leisure”). The Portuguese form may indicate a semi-learned influence on the phonetic aspects of the word.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /isˈkɔ.lɐ/, /esˈkɔ.lɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /isˈkɔ.lɐ/, /esˈkɔ.lɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /iʃˈkɔ.lɐ/, /eʃˈkɔ.lɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /esˈkɔ.la/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /(i)ʃˈkɔ.lɐ/

  • (Northeast Brazil) IPA(key): /isˈkɔ.la/
  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔlɐ
  • Hyphenation: es‧co‧la

Noun

[edit]

escola f (plural escolas)

  1. school (institution dedicated to teaching and learning)
    Os alunos estão indo para a escola. ― The students are going to school.
  2. school (an art movement)
  3. school (the followers of a particular doctrine)
  4. school, college (department or institute dedicated to a specific subject area)
    Escola de música. ― Music school.
  5. method or system of teaching
  6. (figurative) experience

Derived terms

[edit]
  • autoescola
  • escola básica
  • escola de samba
  • escola primária
  • escola profissional
  • escola secundária
  • escolágio
  • escolinha (diminutive)
  • jardim-escola

Related terms

[edit]
  • escolar

Descendants

[edit]
  • Kabuverdianu: skola
  • → Gujarati: ઇસ્કોલ (iskol)
  • → Javanese: ꦱꦼꦏꦺꦴꦭꦃ (sekolah)
  • → Konkani: iśkol
    Devanagari script: इश्कोल
    Latin script: iskol
    Kannada script: ಇಶ್ಕೊಲ್
  • ⇒ Malay: sekolah, sek (abbreviation)
    • > Indonesian: sekolah, sek (inherited)
      • → Ternate: skola, sikola
    • → Iban: sekula
  • → Sinhalese: ස්කෝලය (skōlaya)
  • → Tetum: eskola
